config.title: Build typed filter and sort state model

intro.title: Build typed filter and sort state model
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed state model to manage filter and sort options for a list of items. You'll learn how to use TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of your state, ensuring type safety for properties like filter criteria and sort order. The core concept involves modeling application state with explicit types to prevent errors and improve code clarity. You'll work with TypeScript constructs such as interfaces and type annotations to create a robust, maintainable state structure.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building interactive data interfaces like e-commerce product filters, admin dashboards with sorting controls, or analytics panels with user-configurable views. Developers implement typed filter and sort state models to manage user selections for categories, price ranges, or date periods while ensuring data consistency and type safety. For example, a real estate listing site uses this model to let users filter by property type, bedrooms, and location, then sort by price or date—all with compile-time validation preventing runtime errors. Mastering this approach allows you to create robust, maintainable filtering systems that scale with complex application requirements.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define the shape of filter and sort state.
Initialize a typed state object with default values for filtering and sorting.
Implement handler functions to update specific filter and sort properties.
Apply type annotations to ensure state updates are type-safe.
Integrate the typed state model into a simple application structure.
Manipulate the state by calling handlers in response to simulated user actions.
Configure a component to render UI controls bound to the typed state.

steps.title: Import TypeScript types and interfaces
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript file and define the core types and interfaces needed for filter and sort state. Start by creating an interface for FilterState and a type for SortOrder.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword to define FilterState with properties like category and minPrice. Use the 'type' keyword to define SortOrder as a union of string literals.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a FilterState interface with typed properties and a SortOrder type defined as a union type.
successCriteria: FilterState interface is defined with at least two properties, and SortOrder is defined as a union type with at least two string literal values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both FilterState interface and SortOrder type are properly defined with appropriate properties/values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The types aren't defined correctly. Remember to use 'interface' for FilterState and 'type' for SortOrder with proper TypeScript syntax.

steps.title: Define FilterOptions interface
steps.instruction: Define an interface called FilterOptions with properties: category (string), minPrice (number), maxPrice (number), and inStock (boolean).
steps.hint: Create a TypeScript interface with the specified properties and their types. Place it after your existing FilterState interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: A FilterOptions interface with typed properties for category, minPrice, maxPrice, and inStock will be created.
successCriteria: FilterOptions interface exists with all four properties correctly typed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure all four properties (category, minPrice, maxPrice, inStock) are included with correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FilterOptions interface is missing or has incorrect properties/types. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Define SortOptions interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface called SortOptions with two properties: field (string) and direction (string).
steps.hint: Create an interface with the name SortOptions and add the required properties with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a SortOptions interface that defines the structure for sort configuration.
successCriteria: The SortOptions interface is defined with field: string and direction: string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your SortOptions interface has both field and direction properties with string types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The SortOptions interface isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created an interface with the correct name and properties.

steps.title: Create FilterSortState interface
steps.instruction: Define a new interface named FilterSortState that combines both FilterOptions and SortOptions as properties.
steps.hint: Create an interface with two properties: one for filters and one for sort options.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a FilterSortState interface that contains both filter and sort options.
successCriteria: FilterSortState interface is defined with FilterOptions and SortOptions properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your FilterSortState interface has both FilterOptions and SortOptions properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FilterSortState interface should combine both FilterOptions and SortOptions. Try defining an interface with two properties.

steps.title: Define initial state constant
steps.instruction: Create a constant named initialState that implements the FilterSortState interface with default values.
steps.hint: Use the const keyword to declare initialState and assign it an object with properties matching FilterSortState. Provide sensible default values for each property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed initialState constant with default values is defined, ready to be used as the starting state for your filter and sort model.
successCriteria: initialState is declared as a constant, implements FilterSortState, and includes default values for all required properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created initialState, but check that it implements FilterSortState correctly and has default values for all properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The initialState constant is missing or doesn't properly implement the FilterSortState interface with default values.

steps.title: Create updateFilter function
steps.instruction: Define a function named updateFilter that takes current FilterSortState and partial FilterState updates, and returns a new FilterSortState with the filter properties merged.
steps.hint: The function should accept two parameters: state (type FilterSortState) and updates (type Partial<FilterState>). Return a new object with all state properties, but with filter properties updated.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed updateFilter function that properly merges partial filter updates into the full state.
successCriteria: Function updateFilter is defined with correct parameter types (FilterSortState, Partial<FilterState>) and returns FilterSortState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function accepts FilterSortState and Partial<FilterState> parameters and returns a new FilterSortState object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateFilter function is missing or has incorrect type signatures. It should accept FilterSortState and Partial<FilterState> and return FilterSortState.

steps.title: Create updateSort function
steps.instruction: Define a function called updateSort that takes the current FilterSortState and SortOptions as parameters, and returns a new FilterSortState object with the updated sort property.
steps.hint: The function should return a new state object that spreads the current state and updates only the sort property with the provided sort options.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed updateSort function that properly handles sort state updates while maintaining type safety.
successCriteria: The updateSort function is defined with correct parameter types (FilterSortState, SortOptions) and return type (FilterSortState), and returns a new state object with updated sort property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes both parameters with proper types and returns a new FilterSortState object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateSort function needs to be defined with proper TypeScript types for parameters and return value.

steps.title: Create resetState function
steps.instruction: Define a function called resetState that returns the typed initialState constant.
steps.hint: Create a function that returns the initialState you defined earlier. The function should have no parameters and return the FilterSortState type.
steps.expectedOutcome: A resetState function that returns the initialState constant, providing a typed way to reset the filter and sort state.
successCriteria: The resetState function is defined, has no parameters, and returns the initialState constant.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure resetState is a function that returns the initialState constant.
steps.feedbackWrong: The resetState function isn't defined correctly. It should be a function that returns the initialState.

steps.title: Create example data interface
steps.instruction: Define an interface called Product with properties id (number), name (string), category (string), price (number), and inStock (boolean).
steps.hint: Add this interface after your existing interfaces. Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the name and property definitions.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a Product interface that defines the structure of data you can filter and sort.
successCriteria: Product interface is defined with id (number), name (string), category (string), price (number), and inStock (boolean) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure all five properties (id, name, category, price, inStock) are included with the correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Product interface is not properly defined. Check that you're using the 'interface' keyword and defining all required properties with their types.

steps.title: Create demonstration function
steps.instruction: Create a function named demonstrateFilterSort that uses all the typed interfaces and functions you've built to demonstrate the complete filter and sort model. The function should return a string describing the demonstration.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses your interfaces and functions, then returns a descriptive message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named demonstrateFilterSort that uses your typed model and returns a string.
successCriteria: The demonstrateFilterSort function is created, uses your typed interfaces/functions, and returns a string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named demonstrateFilterSort and returns a string that demonstrates using your typed interfaces and functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The demonstration function wasn't created correctly. Create a function named demonstrateFilterSort that uses your typed model and returns a string.
